headline: High: aci’s broad egress and CRM/email access can leak or act on PaddleOCR-processed documents, while shared API-driven workflows create prompt-injection and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest external content via MCP/direct function calls and has broad integration surfaces; PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can output text that aci may treat as instructions if bridged through files or APIs. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from documented surfaces rather than observed interaction.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into aci prompts or MCP inputs, instruction-like text can steer aci tool use.
IF a shared workspace or API pipeline passes OCR text to aci without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all OCR text before passing it to aci.
Strip imperative phrases from OCR output before downstream use.
Require human review for any OCR-derived instruction.
Use a separate, read-only staging folder for OCR artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-safety filtering between OCR and agent prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If documents contain sensitive data and are routed through aci or external APIs, leakage can occur in default workflows. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF documents containing CRM or email data are OCR-processed and then sent through aci-integrated APIs, sensitive content can leave the local boundary.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace, OCR artifacts may expose customer data to downstream network egress.
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before OCR.
Disable network egress for OCR jobs handling customer data.
Use separate workspaces for CRM and document processing.
Review outbound API destinations for OCR outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API actions; PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs. If both are pointed at the same mutable resources, they can race on shared documents or API state. No locking or coordination is documented, so overlapping writes are plausible and should be treated as a default workflow risk.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same document repository or API-backed record set, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF aci and PaddleOCR are run concurrently against shared mutable resources, duplicate or inconsistent updates are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate write target.
Serialize writes with a simple queue.
Mark OCR outputs read-only until reviewed.
Use per-agent API credentials with least privilege.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking on shared records.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can act on CRM/email/calendar data, while PaddleOCR converts documents into machine-readable text. If aci consumes OCR output as authoritative, OCR mistakes or injected text can cascade into emails, CRM updates, or calendar actions. The pathway is plausible from documented roles, but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF OCR text is fed into aci without verification, transcription errors can become downstream actions.
IF aci is allowed to send email or update CRM records from OCR output, a single OCR mistake can propagate widely.
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action.
Show OCR confidence alongside extracted fields.
Limit aci to draft-only mode for OCR-derived tasks.
Compare OCR output against source images for critical fields.
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, calendar, and support data, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated or region-bound document data is OCRed and then routed through aci’s external integrations. No residency or certification details are documented, so the risk is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are processed by PaddleOCR and then sent through aci integrations, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF the same customer data is retained in both agents' logs, deletion requests may not propagate consistently.
mitigations: Classify document data before OCR.
Keep regulated data out of third-party integrations.
Set short retention on OCR artifacts.
Document the data flow for deletion requests.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies across both systems.
